# RcppLDGM <img align="right" width="145" height="120" src="docs/ldgm_logo.png">

RcppLDGM is an incremental R/Rcpp port of `ldgm`, the Python/MATLAB library for
linkage disequilibrium graphical models (LDGMs), with selected GraphLD-style
operator workflows exposed for R users.

LDGMs are sparse and accurate models of linkage disequilibrium (LD) that
accelerate matrix algebra computations in statistical genetics.

Please cite the upstream LDGM paper if you use LDGMs in published work:

> Pouria Salehi Nowbandegani, Anthony Wilder Wohns, Jenna L. Ballard, Eric S.
> Lander, Alex Bloemendal, Benjamin M. Neale, and Luke J. O'Connor (2023)
> _Extremely sparse models of linkage disequilibrium in ancestrally diverse
> association studies_. Nat Genet. DOI: 10.1038/s41588-023-01487-8

Upstream license and attribution notes are preserved in
[`LICENSE.upstream.md`](LICENSE.upstream.md) and [`inst/LICENSE.note`](inst/LICENSE.note).
The R package license is GPL (>= 3).

## Current port status

Implemented and exported today:

- graph primitives: `ldgm_edge_list()`, `ldgm_remove_node()`,
  `ldgm_return_edgelist()`;
- LDGM reduction core: `ldgm_reduce_graph()`;
- SNP-list table slice: `ldgm_make_snplist()`;
- sparse precision/operator layer: multiply, solve, log determinant, Gaussian
  likelihood, BLUP block, inverse diagonal estimates, OpenMP controls;
- GraphLD-style R interfaces for LDGM IO, precision objects, allele/snplist
  merging, BLUP scheduling, and clumping.

Still intentionally incomplete:

- full tree-sequence bricking: upstream `brick_ts()`;
- full brick-haplotype graph construction: upstream `brick_haplo_graph()`;
- end-to-end tree-sequence `make_ldgm()` wiring;
- remaining GraphLD workflows such as graphREML and the XNys inverse-diagonal
  estimator.

See [`docs/rcpp-port-plan.md`](docs/rcpp-port-plan.md) and
[`docs/graphld-port-plan.md`](docs/graphld-port-plan.md) for the interface and
porting plan.

## Validation and conformance

The conformance policy is to compare against artifacts generated by pinned
upstream code or upstream-owned data. Do **not** use hand-authored fake fixtures
as compatibility evidence.

### LDGM upstream goldens

The upstream LDGM golden workflow uses the checked-out Python `ldgm/` package and
`tests/utility_functions.py` constructors to generate artifacts under
`.sync/ldgm-goldens`:

```sh
make upstream-python
make upstream-ldgm-conformance
```

This regenerates upstream artifacts with:

```sh
.sync/ldgm-python/bin/python tools/generate-upstream-ldgm-goldens.py --out .sync/ldgm-goldens
```

and checks them with:

```sh
RCPP_LDGM_UPSTREAM_GOLDENS=.sync/ldgm-goldens Rscript tools/check-upstream-ldgm-goldens.R
```

Current default upstream examples are valid mutated tree-sequence constructors
from the pinned upstream test suite:

- `single_tree_ts_n2_2_mutations`
- `single_tree_ts_mutation_n3`
- `multiple_snps_branch`
- `figure_one_example`
- `gils_example_tree`
- `single_tree_all_samples_one_mutation_n3`
- `supplementary_example`
- `triangle_example`
- `two_tree_mutation_ts`
- `two_tree_two_mrcas`

The checker validates both:

1. `ldgm_reduce_graph()` against upstream reduced graph edge lists; and
2. `ldgm_make_snplist()` against upstream `ldgm.make_snplist()` outputs.

Expected success message:

```text
Upstream ldgm golden conformance check passed for 10 example(s).
```

The generated `.sync/ldgm-goldens` directory is intentionally excluded from the R
package build; it is reproducible validation evidence, not package data.

### GraphLD upstream smoke data

When `.sync/graphld/data/test` is available, run:

```sh
RCPP_LDGM_GRAPHLD_DATA=.sync/graphld/data/test Rscript tools/check-upstream-graphld-data.R
```

Optional BLUP/clump smoke paths can be enabled with:

```sh
RCPP_LDGM_GRAPHLD_MAX_BLOCKS=1 \
RCPP_LDGM_GRAPHLD_BLUP=true \
RCPP_LDGM_GRAPHLD_CLUMP=true \
Rscript tools/check-upstream-graphld-data.R
```

### R package gates

Core package checks are:

```sh
make warn-test
R CMD build .
R CMD check --no-manual RcppLDGM_0.0.0.9000.tar.gz
```

The project target `warn-test` runs tinytest with `options(warn = 2)`, so R
warnings become failures. The compiled code path is expected to build without
warning-suppression flags in `src/Makevars`.

Latest audited local validation on 2026-05-07:

- tinytest: 109 results, all OK;
- upstream LDGM conformance: 10 examples passed for reduction and SNP-list
  outputs;
- `R CMD build .`: 0 warnings;
- `R CMD check --no-manual RcppLDGM_0.0.0.9000.tar.gz`: `Status: OK`, 0
  WARNING, 0 NOTE.
